items.q: Why do today's agents relearn the same things every session?
items.a: They only learn **in context**, from skill files and the codebase, not **in their weights**.

items.q: What knowledge do agents miss that employees pick up?
items.a: **Latent institutional knowledge**: preferences, friction points, heuristics and the **real org chart**.

items.q: What belongs in context vs in the weights?
items.a: Explicit **rules** go in context; repeated **patterns** have to **earn their way** into the weights.

items.q: What is Will Brown's starting point for continual learning?
items.a: **Evals as test cases**, built from the **traces** you collect in normal use.

items.q: How do you get routing labels?
items.a: Run the **big and small model** on the same task and judge if **the small one was as good**.
A model that learns **how a human approves or rejects** actions in a given situation.

items.q: Why should agents generate small approval widgets?
items.a: They make decisions easy for humans and turn each answer into a **clean training label**.

items.q: What does Brown's nightly loop look like?
items.a: Review proposed experiments and flagged issues, then **train overnight** on **idle inference capacity**.

items.q: What's the ladder toward self-improving organizations?
What did a partner pay to train its own knowledge-work model?
items.a: About **$300K**, roughly the cost of **one hire**.
